messages:
jamal: Not sure if folks saw the overnight spike — we had ~130 tiny GPU pods stuck Pending and a cascade of evictions in ap-southeast1a. filing notes here for triage.
anya: Ugh. Any obvious root? warmpool capacity or scheduler churn?
mike: I pulled the event stream — most pods failed with InsufficientGPUs after a batch of nodes were drained during a maintenance window.
sofia: We drained 6 old racks (nv4p) and replaced with nv5p. New nodes have label gpu.family=ampere-v5. Scheduler affinity rules were recently tightened to prefer same-family packing.
jamal: That label tightening is the suspect imo — tiny pods have podAffinity to same-gpu-family to avoid nvlink mismatch, but the new nodes are being treated as incompatible for tiny-gang co-packing. Lots of tiny pods can't find a matching neighbor so they sit pending.
anya: Can you paste the kubectl describe for one of the stuck pods?
jamal: Sure — snippet:
```
Events:
  Type     Reason             Age   From               Message
  ----     ------             ----  ----               -------
  Normal   Scheduled          5m    default-scheduler  Successfully assigned default/train-87 to node-ampere-v5-03
  Warning  FailedScheduling   5m    default-scheduler  0/20 nodes are available: 20 InsufficientGPUs.
```
mike: Scheduler logs show the pod passed nodeSelectors but failed the custom "family-match" predicate because there were no other pods on the target node matching the team's affinity threshold. Our predicate requires >=1 sibling to avoid tiny gang scatter.
sofia: Right — that predicate was added to reduce cross-generation NVLink failures for large jobs, but it backfired for small single-gpu tasks.
infra-bot: maintenance: nodes drained: rack-apse1-nv4p-{01..06} by ops (1725550000). Autoscaler scaled up 4 nv5p nodes.
anya: Autoscaler only spun up 4 nodes while 6 were drained — expected because reserved capacity cap. That gap led to tight packing and then fragmentation.
jamal: Two simultaneous issues then: (1) overstrict family-match predicate causing pods to be picky, (2) warm pool/autoscaler not replacing capacity fast enough so pods queue up and eviction churn increases.
mike: Quick mitigation idea: relax predicate for pods with resource request <=1 GPU for next 2 hours. Also scale up warmpool target by +8 for the AZ.
sofia: Agreed. I'll open a canary change: set family-match to prefer (score) instead of hard predicate for small pods. jamal, can you push the autoscaler bump? we have some reserved headroom in budget.
jamal: On it. Pushed tentative autoscaler bump to target +8 minimum for ap-southeast1a — monitor CPU/GPU utilization. Patch to scheduler: change map from "RequireSameFamily=true" to "PreferSameFamilyWeight=5" for requests <=1 GPU.
anya: After the bump we should see pending drop and eviction rate normalize. Keep an eye on cross-generation failures though — we relaxed a safety.
mike: Rolling out the change now to canary schedulers in ap-southeast1a (2 nodes). If stable for 10m, we'll roll the rest.
sofia: Also let's add a telemetry check: fraction of tiny pods waiting >30s due to family-match. If it goes back under 1% we can keep the relaxed rule.
infra-bot: deploy: scheduler-canary-apse1 updated (1725556000).
jamal: Early numbers: pending tiny pods down from 130 -> 28 in 6m. Evictions reduced from ~40/hr -> ~6/hr. Good signal.
anya: 👍 cost note — bumping warm pool by +8 will add ~0.9k USD/day in ap-southeast1. We should revert after stabilization.
sofia: We'll set a follow-up alert to auto-scale the warmpool back down 30m after steady state.
mike: Long-term: consider switching predicate to a soft-scoring model with topology awareness and a fallback fast-path for single-GPU pods. Also review reserved capacity vs burst in this AZ to avoid manual bumps.
jamal: Filed follow-ups: GH#1245 schedule scoring long-term, and OPS ticket to review reserved capacity thresholds. Will update thread with postmortem once numbers settle.
anya: Thanks everyone. tagging infra-oncall for visibility. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: alert: oncall notified (1725557200).
